external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders
external_entities.notes: Shoppers use email and password and receive a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out.

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that sends payment settlement webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that serves the storefront, accepts shopper orders, and receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: It is the only thing exposed to the internet. It handles shopper email/password sign-in and session cookies. MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that reads and writes orders and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The worker uses a password supplied through an environment variable. The gRPC caller is intended to be only the storefront API, but the call has no authentication.

processes.name: orders-db
processes.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
processes.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
processes.notes: The order service accesses it with a single application account having full read/write access.

processes.name: receipt archive
processes.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
processes.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
processes.notes: The receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

processes.name: browse storefront
processes.description: Shopper browsing interaction with the storefront API.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: Shopper browsing interaction with the storefront API.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Shopper signs in to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie
data_flows.notes: MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts yet.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Shopper places an order through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service to submit a shopper order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read-write records
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes order records in the orders database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The application account has full read/write access. Its password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: Receipt identifying the order written and the order service that wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a payment-settlement webhook to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Payment settlement notification identifying an order as paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The orders database is confidential because it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values, which are personal and payment-related data.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is confidential because it contains completed-order receipts and order identifiers.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the archive contains receipts for completed orders and records which order was written.
